small_guidance:
- Shared memory blew up because BLOCK_OC=64 × BLOCK_HW=256 × num_stages=3 fp32 accumulator plus tiles is too large; drop to BLOCK_OC=32, BLOCK_HW=128, num_stages=2 (or BLOCK_OC=64/BLOCK_HW=64) so the accumulator fits well under 101 KB.
- Reduce BLOCK_IC to 32 and num_stages to 2 to cut pipelined operand buffers; wrap configs in `triton.autotune` over (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_HW, BLOCK_IC, num_warps, num_stages) so the tuner can find a feasible point automatically.
- Replace the `atomic_add` into pooled with a 2-stage reduction (one kernel writes per-(n,oc,hw-tile) partials, a tiny second kernel sums hw tiles) to avoid contention and allow smaller HW tiles without losing throughput.
large_guidance:
- Rather than gathering the full ConvTranspose2d output and summing it, implement the fused conv-transpose + global-mean as a scatter-style accumulator where each program owns a tile of (N, OC) and loops over input (IC, IH, IW), accumulating `Σ_{ih,iw,kh,kw} x[n,ic,ih,iw] * w[ic,oc,kh,kw] * count(ih+kh, iw+kw is in-bounds) / (OH*OW)`. Since the mean collapses all spatial positions, the per-(oc) result is `(1/HW) Σ_ic w_eff[ic,oc] · Σ_spatial x[n,ic,...]` ONLY if you treat boundary kernel positions correctly — but that is an algebraic shortcut and is forbidden. Instead, keep spatial loops explicit but tile over (N, OC tile) × (input spatial tile) so each program does a real GEMM-shaped accumulation; one program per (n, oc-tile) doing a streaming reduction over (ic, ih, iw) per (kh, kw) keeps shared-memory needs tiny.
- Switch to channels-last input layout (NHWC) so the IC dimension is the contiguous GEMM-K and tl.dot tiles coalesce; preconvert x and weight once in `__init__`/forward prologue.
- Fuse the add-bias + logsumexp + ×10 epilogue into the same kernel by having each program emit its (n, oc) partials to a small per-n scratch of size OC, then a second tiny kernel of grid=(N,) does the logsumexp; or, if OC ≤ 128 fits in registers, keep all OC accumulators live in one persistent program per N and finish the entire pipeline in a single kernel launch.
